title.narrative: YEM038N Yemen Joint Response 2024-2026

description.promeva:title: Description (English)
description.narrative: This is a 3-year Yemen Joint Response (YJR), consisting of 7 DRA members and 13 partners (12 local and 1 international). The YJR 2024-2026 has been developed in line with the priority locations, sectors, activities and approaches defined in the YJR Protracted Crisis Mechanism (PCM) guidelines, a collaborative effort with partner organizations. It was shaped by the discerned needs and gaps, ascertained through individual needs assessments, secondary data sources, and cluster consultations. This comprehensive three-year YJR initiative is primarily focused on the governorates of Sa’ada, Hajjah, Marib, Taiz, Lahj, Aden, and Al Dhale’e. These areas represent the highest concentration of individuals in need of humanitarian assistance, where the most severe needs and gaps persist. The response proposes an integrated Health, Food Security and Livelihood (FSL), Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Protection, Multi-Purpose Cash (MPC), and protection mainstreaming programme. The objective is to provide multifaceted, life-saving humanitarian support to those in need, prioritising the most vulnerable population. Simultaneously, it aims to facilitate early recovery and enhance the resilience of communities affected by the conflict in Yemen. It is essential that all activities are designed to ensure equitable access to assistance for women, girls, boys, men, and people with disabilities (PWD).

title.narrative: Number of people provided with resources to protect and start rebuilding livelihood assets

comment.narrative: During the second quarter of 2025, CARE launched intensive efforts to prepare for the second phase of the Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) program. By May, coordination efforts successfully identified the need to retarget the same Health Unit in AlGalilah village - originally targeted in 2024 - for the new phase of the Community Food-for-Work (CFW) program. CARE dedicated its efforts to building strong partnerships with local communities through dialogue sessions held with the community committee and local leaders. These meetings facilitated an exchange of perspectives on the project’s goals and led to the selection of the community asset to be rehabilitated: constructing a fence around the health unit that CARE had built in 2024. By June, the registration process had begun for 50 beneficiaries to participate in the CFW activity. The verification process is scheduled to take place in July 2025. Additionally, all Bills of Quantities (BoQs) for the CFW activity have been prepared and submitted to the Supply Chain Department. For Q3 of 2025, the verification process for the 50 registered beneficiaries achieved and completed in July 2025. The targeted beneficiaries started the work in 6 Aug 2025 at the work site to build and constructing a fence 30m*30m around the health unit that CARE had built in 2024 in AlGalilah village in AlDhale’e district. Until end of Sep 2025, The 50 beneficiaries worked 2 months and the achievement is around 50%. The remaining works will be completed and achieved during the coming two months. The targeted 50 HH- 390 Indvi (100 M, 125 W, 95 B, 70 G) received one round with an amount 188000 YER per month per beneficiary. The first round was distributed in 9 Sep 2025.

title.narrative: Number of primary health care consultations

comment.narrative: Since the beginning of the project, a total of 29,124 individuals (7340 boys, 7635 girls, 4581 men, and 9568 women) have received primary health consultations across targeted static and mobile health facilities. During the second quarter of 2025 (Q2), 8,422 beneficiaries (2,354 boys, 2,456 girls, 1,211 men, and 2,401 women) accessed primary health services in the supported facilities. • Of this total, 4,559 individuals (1,346 boys, 1,375 girls, 774 men, and 1,064 women) received services at the Al-Gubara static health center in Qatabah District. • An additional 2,313 beneficiaries (552 boys, 586 girls, 279 men, and 896 women) were reached through the mobile health clinic operating under Diversity’s supervision. ________________________________________ Crisis Modifier Intervention – Measles Outbreak Response In response to the recent measles outbreak, CARE—through Diversity—deployed two mobile health clinics to cover (Al-Shuaib District, Qa'atabah District, and Al-Dhalea Districts) Each clinic was staffed with qualified health professionals and provided integrated services, including: • Active case detection • Vaccination and symptom management • Distribution of essential medications (e.g., analgesics, antibiotics, and Vitamin A supplements) In June 2025 alone, the mobile teams reached 1,550 individuals (495 girls, 456 boys, 441 women, and 158 men). Furthermore, 30 trained female community health volunteers conducted health awareness sessions across three districts. These sessions emphasized the importance of immunization and included key messages on: • Measles prevention and early symptom recognition • Reporting procedures and community-based surveillance • Hygiene promotion and boosting vaccine acceptance These activities collectively enhanced community resilience and strengthened the local health response capacity against vaccine-preventable disease outbreaks.

Since the start of the project, a total of 36,555 individuals (9,247 boys, 9,656 girls, 5,808 men, and 11,844 women) have received primary health consultations, including reproductive health (RH) and immunization (EPI) services, across targeted static and mobile health facilities.
During Quarter 3 of 2025, 7,458 beneficiaries (1,933 boys, 2,022 girls, 1,227 men, and 2,276 women) accessed primary health services in the supported facilities:
- 4,692 individuals (1,359 boys, 1,375 girls, 793 men, and 1,165 women) received services at Al-Gubara static health center in Qatabah District. - 2,766 beneficiaries (574 boys, 647 girls, 434 men, and 111 women) were reached through the mobile health clinic operating under Diversity’s supervision.
These services have significantly improved access to essential healthcare for vulnerable populations, ensured timely prevention and treatment of illnesses, enhanced maternal and child health outcomes, and strengthened trust in local health facilities. The availability of integrated RH and EPI services has also reduced the risk of vaccine-preventable diseases, supported safe motherhood, and contributed to overall community health resilience.

title.narrative: Number of health facilities rehabilitated

comment.narrative: BoQs and desings were approved by MoPHP. In coordination with local authority and health office in Al-Dhalea, the activity of health facility constrction is on going in Al-Galelah area in Al-Dhalea district, In collaboration with the local authority and health office in Al-Dhalea, the work is going smoothly with FSL team through cash for work for the building foundations.

Construction activities commenced in March 2025, and by the end of June 2025 , major structural components—including the foundation, walls, and roof—were successfully completed. The remaining works, including interior and exterior finishing works, are expected to be finalized between August and September 2025

Q 3 2025 Construction activities began in March 2025, and all remaining works, including interior and exterior finishes, were completed in September 2025, marking the end of the construction phase. The health center will open its doors to beneficiaries once the FSL team completes the surrounding fence through cash for work, scheduled for December 2025. CARE will equip the facility with essential medical equipment and furniture through the MES project, ensuring it is fully operational. This support will enable the health center to provide quality primary healthcare, reproductive health, and immunization services, enhancing access to essential care for women, children, IDPs, and other vulnerable populations in the surrounding communities.
